evals.prompt: Perform a security audit of a Python Flask web application for a mid-sized fintech company. The application handles user authentication, account management, and payment processing. It uses Flask 2.3, SQLAlchemy 2.0 with PostgreSQL, Redis for session caching, and integrates with Stripe for payments. The codebase is located at /home/user/projects/fintech-app/ and includes the following key files: app.py (main application with routes), models.py (database models), auth.py (authentication logic), payments.py (Stripe integration), and config.py (configuration). The application has approximately 5,000 lines of code. Identify all security vulnerabilities, classify them by severity using CVSS v3.1, and provide a comprehensive audit report with detailed findings, evidence, and remediation recommendations.
evals.expected_output: A comprehensive security audit report in markdown format containing: (1) Executive Summary with overall risk rating and findings count by severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low/Informational), (2) Scope and Methodology section listing audited components, tools used (Bandit, Semgrep, Safety, manual review), and standards referenced (OWASP Top 10, CWE), (3) Findings Summary table with ID, Title, Severity, and Category columns, (4) Detailed Findings section where each finding includes: a unique Reference ID, concise Title, Severity rating, CVSS v3.1 score with full vector string, CWE classification, Description of the vulnerability, Root cause analysis, Affected component with specific file and line numbers, Evidence (code excerpts or tool output demonstrating the issue), Business impact assessment, and specific actionable Remediation steps. Expected vulnerabilities to identify include: SQL injection via unparameterized queries in models.py, hardcoded secrets in config.py, missing CSRF protection on state-changing endpoints, insecure session management with predictable session IDs, IDOR vulnerabilities in account endpoints allowing access to other users' data, verbose error messages leaking stack traces, missing rate limiting on authentication endpoints, and insecure deserialization. Each finding must include a proof-of-concept or concrete exploit path. The report should conclude with a Risk Assessment matrix and prioritized Recommendations list.

evals.prompt: Audit a Solidity smart contract for a decentralized lending protocol on Ethereum. The protocol allows users to deposit ETH as collateral and borrow against it at a 75% LTV ratio. The main contract is LendingPool.sol (approximately 800 lines, Solidity 0.8.19) which includes functions for deposit, borrow, repay, and liquidate. It uses Chainlink price feeds for ETH/USD pricing and implements a liquidation mechanism with a 5% bonus for liquidators. The contract uses OpenZeppelin's Ownable and ReentrancyGuard. There is also an InterestRateModel.sol contract that calculates dynamic interest rates based on utilization. The protocol has $50M TVL and has been live for 3 months. Perform a thorough security audit identifying all vulnerabilities, classifying them using the Immunefi severity scale, and provide a detailed audit report with evidence and remediation guidance.
evals.expected_output: A professional smart contract security audit report in markdown format containing: (1) Executive Summary with overall risk rating (Critical/High/Medium/Low per Immunefi scale) and findings count by severity, (2) Scope and Methodology section listing contracts audited (LendingPool.sol, InterestRateModel.sol), tools used (Slither, Aderyn, Mythril, manual review), and standards referenced (SWC Registry, Immunefi), (3) Findings Summary table with ID, Title, Severity, and Category columns, (4) Detailed Findings section where each finding includes: a unique Reference ID, concise Title, Immunefi severity rating, SWC classification, Description of the vulnerability, Root cause analysis, Affected contract and function with specific line numbers, Evidence (code excerpts, tool output, or transaction-level proof-of-concept demonstrating exploitability), Business impact assessment including potential financial loss quantification, and specific actionable Remediation steps with code-level fix suggestions. Expected vulnerabilities to identify include: oracle manipulation risk from using spot price instead of TWAP, liquidation logic that can be front-run for MEV extraction, interest rate model edge cases causing insolvency at extreme utilization, reentrancy in liquidate function despite ReentrancyGuard (cross-function reentrancy), precision loss in interest calculations, missing access control on critical functions, and griefing vectors in liquidation. Each finding must include a concrete exploit scenario or proof-of-concept. The report should include an Invariants section documenting protocol invariants and whether they hold, a Risk Assessment matrix, and prioritized Recommendations.

evals.prompt: Conduct a mixed web2/web3 security assessment for a decentralized exchange (DEX) platform. The system consists of: (1) A React/TypeScript frontend at /home/user/projects/dex-frontend/ that interacts with smart contracts via ethers.js v6, including components for token swapping, liquidity provision, and wallet connection; (2) A Node.js/Express backend API at /home/user/projects/dex-backend/ that provides price quotes, transaction history, and user preferences, using PostgreSQL and Redis; (3) Solidity smart contracts at /home/user/projects/dex-contracts/ including a ConstantProductAMM.sol (Uniswap V2 fork, ~300 lines), Router.sol (~200 lines), and ERC20 token contracts. The platform has $10M TVL and processes approximately $500K daily volume. The assessment should cover the full stack: smart contract vulnerabilities, backend API security, frontend security issues (including wallet integration risks), and cross-component attack vectors. Identify all security issues, classify by severity, and provide a comprehensive audit report.
evals.expected_output: A comprehensive full-stack security audit report in markdown format containing: (1) Executive Summary with overall risk rating and findings count by severity across all layers (smart contracts, backend API, frontend), (2) Scope and Methodology section listing all components audited (smart contracts, backend API, frontend), tools used (Slither, Mythril, Semgrep, Bandit, npm audit, manual review), and standards referenced (OWASP Top 10, SWC Registry, Immunefi), (3) Architecture Overview section documenting the system's trust boundaries, data flows, and component interactions, (4) Findings Summary table with ID, Title, Severity, Category, and Layer (Contract/API/Frontend/Cross-component) columns, (5) Detailed Findings section where each finding includes: a unique Reference ID, concise Title, Severity rating, appropriate classification (CWE for web2, SWC for web3), Description, Root cause, Affected component with specific file and line numbers, Evidence (code excerpts, tool output, or proof-of-concept), Business impact, and specific Remediation steps. Expected findings include: smart contract vulnerabilities (reentrancy, slippage protection gaps, fee-on-transfer token handling, price manipulation via sandwich attacks), backend API vulnerabilities (SQL injection in price query endpoints, missing authentication on admin endpoints, rate limiting gaps, CORS misconfiguration allowing arbitrary origins), frontend vulnerabilities (XSS via token name injection, wallet signature phishing risks, private key exposure in localStorage, missing transaction deadline leading to stale execution), and cross-component attack vectors (price oracle manipulation combining frontend slippage settings with contract MEV, replay attacks across chains, signature malleability in meta-transactions). Each finding must include a concrete exploit path demonstrating how the vulnerability can be exploited in the context of the full system. The report should include a Threat Model using STRIDE methodology, a Risk Assessment matrix, and prioritized Recommendations organized by layer.
